newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 30.

text.p: There are 62 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- SING TAO DAILY said that Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa should try to find a balance when making the final decision over amending two civil rights ordinances, so as to maintain both social stability and citizens' rights. The Federation of Trade Union's suggestion to ban local political groups from receiving mainland funding showed that the pro-Beijing group was open-minded.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said that the public consultation over the proposal to amend two civil rights ordinances had been successful. It said that Tung should stick to his principles and take into consideration Hong Kong people's correct opinions when deciding whether or how to amend the two ordinances.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said there has been little time for debating the far-reaching issue of changing the Societies and Public Order ordinances, and the decisions which follow will have a profound effect on Hong Kong. Only if Tung can demonstrate that Hong Kong needed curbs on its freedom should he move to impose them. Undiluted, these changes will dishearten Hong Kong people and send negative signals abroad.
